issues.description: Method name inconsistency for the same conceptual operation (total number of students). The problem statement text instructs students to implement a method named `get_total_number_of_students()` (snake_case) while the UML diagram in the problem statement, the template comments, and the solution use the Java-style camelCase name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This mismatch can confuse students about which exact method name/signature to implement and may lead to failing automated checks if they follow the wrong name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to refer to the Java camelCase method name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (replace `get_total_number_of_students()`), and ensure any textual references, examples, and hints use the same identifier. Alternatively, explicitly state that either name is acceptable and show the exact expected method signature (e.g., public int getTotalNumberOfStudents()).
